meta.title: Who originally recorded "Wagon Wheel"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Darius Rucker. Old Crow Medicine Show released it in February 2004 on Nettwerk - and an earlier 2001 EP recording is listed too.
meta.ogDescription: Darius Rucker's 2013 No. 1 is a cover. Old Crow Medicine Show recorded it first; Bob Dylan and Ketch Secor wrote it.

answer.label: Not a Darius Rucker original — Old Crow Medicine Show got there first, and earlier than 2004
answer.originalArtistDates: Formed 1998 · American old-time string band, Harrisonburg, Virginia
answer.sourceLine: Darius Rucker’s 2013 Capitol Nashville single is the version most people have heard, and many assume he originated it. He did not: Old Crow Medicine Show released it as a single on 10 February 2004, ahead of their Nettwerk album O.C.M.S. on 24 February 2004. The song is credited to Bob Dylan and Ketch Secor — Dylan sketched the chorus at the 1973 Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid sessions, and Secor wrote verses around it years later. One wrinkle the usual account skips: MusicBrainz lists an earlier Old Crow recording of the song on a self-issued 2001 EP, Troubles Up and Down the Road, so 2004 is the famous first release rather than certainly the first recording.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Nettwerk
original.released: Issued as a single on 10 February 2004 and as a track on the band’s Nettwerk debut album O.C.M.S. on 24 February 2004; recorded in 2003 at RCA Studio B in Nashville with producer David Rawlings. MusicBrainz additionally lists a recording of the song on a self-issued Old Crow EP, Troubles Up and Down the Road, dated 24 October 2001.
original.charted: No mainstream chart entry on release — it spread by word of mouth rather than radio. It first shows up in the trades in the week of 20 March 2013, riding the Rucker single: 15,000 copies sold, No. 28 on Country Digital Songs. It was certified platinum in April 2013 and three-times platinum by November 2023.
original.cover: Darius Rucker, Capitol Nashville, released 7 January 2013 from the album True Believers. No. 1 on Hot Country Songs and Country Airplay, No. 1 on Canada Country, No. 15 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 23 on the Canadian Hot 100. Grammy for Best Country Solo Performance, January 2014; certified 11× platinum.
trail: The song’s Wikipedia entry dates the Old Crow single to 10 February 2004 and the Rucker single to 7 January 2013 — Wagon Wheel (song) ↗.
The album page confirms the 24 February 2004 Nettwerk release, David Rawlings’ production and the RCA Studio B sessions — O.C.M.S. ↗.
Rolling Stone traces the chorus to Dylan’s 1973 Pat Garrett sessions and the bootleg Critter Fuqua carried home from London — Rolling Stone ↗.
The earlier, unlabelled 2001 EP that complicates the tidy version of the story — Troubles Up and Down the Road on MusicBrainz ↗.

authors.name: Old Crow Medicine Show
authors.heading: Old Crow Medicine Show
authors.bio: A busking string band that formed in 1998 and toured Canada on a self-made cassette before anyone was listening. In 2000 Doc Watson’s daughter heard them playing outside a drugstore in Boone, North Carolina and brought her father over — the endorsement that opened doors. Their Nettwerk debut O.C.M.S., produced by David Rawlings and cut at RCA Studio B in Nashville in 2003, carried the song that would define them.

authors.name: Darius Rucker
authors.heading: Darius Rucker
authors.metaLine: American singer · Hootie & the Blowfish frontman turned country artist
authors.bio: Rucker cut the song for his third country album, True Believers, and released it on Capitol Nashville on 7 January 2013. It went to No. 1 on Hot Country Songs and Country Airplay, reached No. 15 on the Hot 100, won the Grammy for Best Country Solo Performance in January 2014, and was certified 11× platinum. It is a genuinely fine record — the only error is chronological.

authors.name: Bob Dylan and Ketch Secor
authors.heading: Bob Dylan and Ketch Secor
authors.metaLine: Credited co-writers · a 1973 sketch finished decades later
authors.bio: Dylan recorded an unfinished, untitled fragment during the 1973 Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid sessions; bootleg collectors later filed it as “Rock Me, Mama.” Old Crow’s Critter Fuqua picked up a bootleg of those sessions in London as a teenager and passed it to Ketch Secor, who built full verses around the chorus. The two are credited as co-writers on a fifty-fifty split, and Old Crow have said they share the royalties evenly with Dylan.

misattribution.heading: What’s actually true
misattribution.intro: Rucker’s 2013 single is so much bigger than the record it came from that the original has largely been overwritten. Here is the order of events.

items.who: Darius Rucker wrote and originated “Wagon Wheel”
items.why: His version was released on 7 January 2013 on Capitol Nashville, nine years after Old Crow Medicine Show’s single, and he is not a credited writer.
Released as a single on 10 February 2004 and on the Nettwerk album O.C.M.S. on 24 February 2004, recorded in 2003 at RCA Studio B with producer David Rawlings.

MusicBrainz lists a recording of the song as track six of a self-issued EP, Troubles Up and Down the Road, dated 24 October 2001 with no label. Same band, so the answer to “who first” does not change — but we could not confirm that 2001 date against a primary or reference source, so we do not present 2004 as certainly the first time it was committed to tape.
Dylan cut the chorus as an unfinished sketch at the 1973 Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid sessions; Secor wrote the verses around it, and the two are credited on a fifty-fifty split.

misattribution.truthLine: Old Crow Medicine Show recorded it first — issued in February 2004, and possibly on a self-released EP as early as 2001. Darius Rucker’s 2013 hit is a cover.

context.heading: Why the cover ate the original
lead: Old Crow Medicine Show’s version was never a radio record. It had no mainstream chart entry in 2004; it spread the slow way — campfires, dorm rooms, wedding bands, open mics — until it was effectively folk repertoire before most listeners knew whose record it was. That is exactly the condition in which a big-label cover can arrive and look like the source.

When Darius Rucker released it on Capitol Nashville in January 2013 with country radio behind it, the song finally had a version that arrived everywhere at once. Rucker’s record went to No. 1 country and was certified 11× platinum. The original benefited too — in the week of 20 March 2013, with Rucker dominating, Old Crow’s 2004 recording sold 15,000 copies and ranked No. 28 on Country Digital Songs — but by then it read to most people as a cover of the hit rather than the other way round.
detailsBody: February 1973 — Bob Dylan records an unfinished, untitled sketch during the Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid sessions; bootleggers later label it “Rock Me, Mama.”
Late 1990s — Critter Fuqua obtains a bootleg of those sessions in London and shares it with Ketch Secor, who writes verses around Dylan’s chorus. The band play it from their teens.
24 October 2001 — MusicBrainz dates a self-issued Old Crow Medicine Show EP, Troubles Up and Down the Road, carrying a recording of the song. No label is listed.
2003 — the band record the song with producer David Rawlings at RCA Studio B, Nashville.
10 February 2004 — released as a single; the album O.C.M.S. follows on Nettwerk on 24 February 2004.
15 June 2012 — Nathan Carter’s version is released and becomes a long-running hit in Ireland and the UK.
7 January 2013 — Darius Rucker’s Capitol Nashville single is released; it tops Hot Country Songs and Country Airplay and wins a Grammy in January 2014.
2013 and after — the Old Crow recording is certified platinum in April 2013 and three-times platinum by November 2023.
context.pull: A song can be everywhere for a decade and still have no famous author.
